question.leadin: Answer these questions about leaders with titles in common.
question.text: Give the title last held by Nicholas II of Russia before he was killed in 1918.
question.clue: It's not in Germany, but one holder of this title issued the Anti-Semitic May Laws, which prohibited the creation of new towns by Jews.

swap.text: This mystic and advisor to Nicholas II avoided being executed along with the imperial family because he had already been poisoned, stabbed, shot, and drowned.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Bolshevik Revolution.
question.text: The Bolsheviks revolted against this Prime Minister of Russia's provisional government, which had already deposed the Tsar in March of 1917.
question.clue: Brusilov also led the failed 1917 June Offensive planned by this leader of the Provisional Government, who was targeted in the Kornilov Affair. This man issued Order No. 8 and fled after the October Revolution.

swap.text: Following the death of Nicholas I, this man took the throne of Russia and enacted reforms in the military following the Crimean War, although he is better known for freeing the Serfs.
swap.clue: During his reign, he re-established the Diet of Finland and elevated Finnish to a national language.

question.text: Alongside serving as the Prince of Novgorod, Nevsky served as the Grand Prince of this city. This city was the center of a namesake "Rus" until it was sacked by the Golden Horde.
question.clue: A ruler of this city militarily supported the Byzantine emperor Basil II, which resulted in the formation of the Varangian Guard, in exchange for marrying Basil II's sister Anna.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about common phrases in Obama administration foreign policy.
swap.text: During her term as Secretary of State, Hillary Clinton claimed credit for the "reset", the easing of tensions in 2009 between the US and this foreign nation.
swap.clue: The mostly-defunct political party Yabloko is a protest voice in this country.

question.text: The war effectively came to an end after the Malakoff Redoubt was captured in a siege of this most populous city on the Crimean Peninsula.
question.clue: William Howard Russell coined a name for troops who fought off an attack on this city by General Liprandi.

swap.text: This final Russian czar came to the imperial throne in 1894 after the untimely death of his conservative father, Alexander III.
swap.clue: Most of this ruler's fleet was lost in the Battle of Tsushima in a war that ended as a humiliating loss to Japan.

question.text: This capital of the USSR was the site of the 1980 Olympics, as well as frequent "physical culture" parades in Red Square.
question.clue: This city traces its history to a post founded by Yuri of the Long Arm.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a historical figure.
swap.text: Mazepa served as the hetman of these fiercely independent horsemen who lived along the Don river and often served in the Czar's armies.
swap.clue: A five-year siege of Orenburg was done by one of these people named Yemelyan Pugachev.

question.text: The first of these plans imposed grain quotas as part of agricultural collectivisation and rapid industrialisation and overturned many policies of the NEP. These Soviet centralised economic plans were announced regularly.
question.answer: Five Year Plans of the USSR

swap.leadin: This man conducted an impromptu debate with President Nixon in 1959 in an American model kitchen.
swap.text: Name this Soviet premier, who denounced Stalin's cult of personality in the "Secret Speech."
swap.clue: He denounced his predecessor in the "Secret Speech," which precipitated a "thaw" named for him.

question.leadin: After this person had him arrested, Jan Chryzostom Pasek ("yahn hree-ZO-stome PAH-sek") possibly made up a story about this person being beaten up by his neighbor after he had an affair with his wife.
question.text: Name this Cossack hetman and Ukrainian national hero. After he learned he was about to be replaced by Alexander Menshikov, this person defected during the Battle of Poltava.
question.clue: This Ukrainian leader sought to reunite his homeland and so he turned against his former ally, Peter I, and joined Charles XII of Sweden. He was defeated at Poltava.

swap.leadin: These people were killed after they participated in the Bezdna Unrest.
swap.text: Identify this class of people who were freed by an 1861 decree during the reign of Alexander II.
swap.clue: An imperial edict by Paul I forbade compelling these people to perform corvee labor on Sundays.

question.leadin: An incident after one of these events was blamed on Illarion Vorontsov-Dashkov frequently sleeping until the late afternoon.
question.text: Around 1,400 people died in a stampede at Khodynka Field when coins and bread commemorating one of these events ran out. At these events, two figures received the Orb and Sceptre as a te deum laudamus was sung.
question.answer: Imperial Coronation of the Russian Emperor

swap.text: Ivan VI reigned for just 13 months as an infant before being overthrown by this person, his cousin. This person, who established the Imperial Moscow University, was the youngest daughter of Peter the Great .
swap.answerHtml: Empress Elizabeth of Russia [or Elizabeth Petrovna, also accept Yelisaveta or Elizaveta ]
swap.clue: Lopukhina's tongue was later torn out for an alleged plot to restore this ruler's predecessor, Ivan VI.

question.text: This Russian tsar demanded that the Livonian confederation pay high taxes and occupied Dorpat and Narva, setting off the Livonian war.
question.answer: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible
question.clue: This son of Basil III prosecuted the Livonian War and suppressed Novgorod. Ruling from 1547 to 1584, this Rurikid was notable for maintaining the oprichina, a secret police force, and being an all-around mean dude.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Russian leaders during the Time of Troubles.
swap.text: This powerful regent controlled Russia during the reign of Tsar Feodor the Bellringer. He later got himself elected Tsar by the zemsky sobor and ruled until his death in 1605.
swap.clue: He promoted his friend the Metropolitan Job, thus resulting in the creation of the Patriarchate, and Job would later convene the comission that made this man tsar.

question.text: The "green army" is the name sometimes given to Aleksandr Antonov's forces during this rebellion. This peasant rebellion took place during the Russian Civil War and was ended by Mikhail Tukhachevsky.
question.clue: This rebellion, which was suppressed with a force of one hundred thousand Red Army troops under Mikhail Tukhachevsky, who used tactics like firing poisonous gas at peasant strongholds.

swap.text: The Russians also had to form a special police unit to combat cannibalism during this battle. Despite enmity between Finland and Russia, Mannerheim refused to commit troops to this operation, which saw the Sinyavin Offensive and Operation Iskra.
swap.clue: One participant in this event was successfully contained by the Karelia fortified region, and one side was supplied by the Ice Road during the winter, with trucks crossing the frozen surface of Lake Ladoga.
